audit_findings.title: Completed Leggett transaction is absent from both the numerator and denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $2.5 billion transaction value, equal to 36.1% of the $6.933 billion base equity value; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Leggett earnings and inherited interest expense are absent from owner earnings, acquisition shares are absent from fully diluted shares, and acquired cash, debt, leases and other senior claims are absent from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We could also issue a significant number of shares of our common stock in the future in connection with acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the September 5 valuation follows the August 26 closing but values the pre-closing business and share claim. The missing business, dilution and senior claims are large enough to change both total equity value and per-share value, although their net direction cannot be established without the closing data.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing 8-K and exchange-ratio calculation, shares actually issued, opening post-acquisition balance sheet, assumed debt and leases, target cash, transaction financing and incremental interest expense; rerun numerator, bridge and denominator on the same post-closing perimeter.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a full-year observation of the Mattress Firm perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: Mattress Firm supplied $3.5054 billion, or 46.9%, of reported 2025 sales; filed full-year pro forma sales exceed reported sales by $267.1 million, or 3.6%; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The $485.5 million owner-earnings anchor capitalizes an eleven-month acquisition stub containing incomplete operating, interest, lease, integration, purchase-accounting and working-capital periods.
audit_findings.evidence: Unless otherwise noted, all of the financial information in this Report is consolidated financial information for the Company, including Mattress Firm's financial results for the period February 5, 2025 through December 31, 2025 (the "stub period").
audit_findings.explanation: The lack of a clean twelve-month observation is demonstrated, but the record does not quantify the missing period's sustainable owner earnings. The filed sales difference alone is modest relative to the valuation, while acquisition accounting and integration effects could move earnings in either direction; materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build a trailing-twelve-month owner-earnings bridge through June 2026 or later, separating the missing Mattress Firm period, full-period interest and rent, purchase-accounting charges, integration spending, working capital and maintenance capital expenditure; rerun using the reconciled full-perimeter anchor.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease investment may bypass the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 finance-lease principal payments were $22.1 million, or 4.6% of the $485.5 million anchor; new finance-lease right-of-use assets were $32.5 million, or 6.7%; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease depreciation is added back through D&A while neither finance-lease principal nor maintenance right-of-use additions are deducted, recurring capital investment is omitted from owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Assets under finance leases are included within property, plant and equipment and represent non-cash investing activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that finance-lease depreciation, principal payments and non-cash asset additions exist, but the supplied valuation does not disclose enough of its owner-earnings bridge to prove an omission. The identified annual amounts are below 7% of the anchor, but their recurring maintenance portion and treatment across the forecast are unknown.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the D&A add-back to finance-lease depreciation and reconcile capital investment to both $22.1 million of principal payments and $32.5 million of new right-of-use assets; deduct the maintenance component once, without double counting lease interest, and rerun if omitted.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-related deferred tax claims are outside the operating history
audit_findings.magnitude: $335.8 million stock-basis-recapture deferred tax liability, equal to 4.8% of base equity value and $1.56 per diluted share if deducted in full immediately
audit_findings.mechanism: A restructuring, disposal or other tax trigger could convert an indefinite-lived deferred tax liability into a cash claim ahead of common equity that is neither represented in historical owner earnings nor separately deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The stock basis recapture and the majority of the intangible asset deferred tax liabilities are indefinite-lived in nature.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is filed and potentially meaningful, but it is described as indefinite-lived and the record establishes neither a probable payment nor its timing. Even a full immediate $335.8 million deduction would reduce the $32.12 base value to approximately $30.56 per share, so the presently identified amount alone would not reverse the valuation conclusion; the trigger remains forward-looking.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-basis-recapture memorandum and acquisition tax schedules identifying legal triggers, expected reversal dates and settlement probabilities; add a probability-weighted bridge deduction or cash-tax forecast only when payment becomes supportable, including any change caused by Leggett.

audit_findings.title: The anchor lacks a disclosed reconciliation of unusually large acquisition costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $114.2 million of acquisition-related costs, equal to 23.5% of the $485.5 million anchor; total filed 2025 operating-income adjustments were $263.8 million, or 54.3% of the anchor; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining genuinely one-time cash charges depresses normalized owner earnings, while adding back recurring restructuring, merchandising-transition or integration spending inflates owner earnings and every forecast and terminal-value cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: In the year ended 2025, we recognized $114.2 million of acquisition-related costs following the Mattress Firm Acquisition, primarily related to one-time business combination accounting and purchase price allocation adjustments, professional fees and restructuring costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing reconciliation is demonstrated, and the disclosed adjustment pool is large relative to the capitalized anchor. The record does not show which amounts entered the $485.5 million calculation or whether they were cash, non-cash or recurring, so direction is mixed; the possible anchor movement is large enough to materially alter the valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete FY2025 owner-earnings bridge from filed net income to $485.5 million, itemizing every acquisition, transaction, business-combination, disposal, disposition and transition adjustment by cash status and recurrence; compare classifications with 2026 Mattress Firm and Leggett integration spending and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Multi-employer pension deficits may create an unrecorded senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 multi-employer retirement-plan expense was $4.1 million, or 0.8% of the anchor; contributions to the two disclosed significant Red Zone plans were $1.7 million and already included 10% surcharges; incremental withdrawal liability unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rehabilitation contributions, higher negotiated rates or withdrawal liabilities would reduce owner earnings or require a bridge deduction ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company participates in several plans which are in the Red Zone for 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Current contributions and disclosed surcharges are already operating expenses and are small relative to the anchor. No withdrawal event, probable incremental payment or estimable withdrawal liability is supplied, so this is a forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current actuarial funded-status notices, rehabilitation schedules, 2026–2027 collective-bargaining terms and employer withdrawal-liability estimates; rerun owner earnings or the bridge if an incremental payment becomes probable and measurable.
